items.title: Ground stop lifted after cargo plane veers off runway at Miami International Airport
items.text:
Miami-Dade deputies responded to a FedEx cargo plane that veered off the runway at Miami International Airport, with no injuries reported.

Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office deputies responded to Miami International Airport Wednesday night after a FedEx cargo plane ran off the runway just before 8:30 p.m. Deputies located the plane, which was occupied by two individuals. There were no injuries reported. All flights coming to and from the airport were grounded for more than an hour. In a statement, the FAA said: "Flights will be resuming shortly at Miami International Airport after FedEx Flight 910 ran off the runway after landing. The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 departed from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis. There are no reports of injuries. The FAA will investigate the incident." This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available. items.title: Florida Woman Loses Her License Over a Miami-Dade Speeding Ticket Tied to a Plate She's Never Had
items.text:
Trish Fancher found out her driver’s license was suspended when her husband tried to renew their plates in September. He called her with the news, and she learned that Florida had suspended her licens...

Trish Fancher found out her driver's license was suspended when her husband tried to renew their plates in September. He called her with the news, and she learned that Florida had suspended her license over an unpaid school-zone speeding ticket she said she knew nothing about.
The ticket came from Miami-Dade County and dated back to 2025. Fancher, who lives in North Fort Myers, told Gulf Coast News that she hadn't been to Miami-Dade in nearly 20 years.
Her first thought was that someone had stolen her identity. She wondered whether another driver had handed an officer a license with her information on it. When she got a copy of the citation, she learned a school-zone camera had recorded the speeding violation.
Fancher filed a motion to get the ticket dismissed and her license reinstated. In the meantime, she had to rely on other people for rides. She figured it would take a few days to sort out. By the fifth week, she told the station, "it was no longer cute."
The citation listed a Nebraska plate with a tag that had expired in 2003. Fancher said she had never been to Nebraska and didn't know anyone from there.
The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office told Gulf Coast News that the vendor had looked up a Florida plate instead of the Nebraska one. The vendor sent that information to Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles, which returned Fancher's information. The sheriff's office described the error as isolated.
Under Florida's school-zone camera law , the first notice goes by mail to the vehicle's registered owner and must include an image of the plate. If the owner takes none of the steps the law allows in response, such as paying or requesting a hearing, a formal traffic citation follows by certified mail.
Once a citation goes unpaid past its deadline, Florida law requires the clerk to notify the state motor vehicle agency, which then issues a suspension order. The ticket in Fancher's case was dismissed, but Gulf Coast News reported that she still had to pay to get her license back.

items.title: 21-Story, 363-Unit 'Spoke Aventura' Planned for 2028 Completion at 2600 N.E. 203rd Street, Miami, Florida
items.text:
Florida YIMBY says "Yes In My Backyard" to positive new development in Florida.

A Boca Raton-based developer has plans for an apartment building under the Live Local Act in Aventura.
Spoke Aventura is slated to measure 21 stories above grade and host 363 apartments – 146 of which (about 40 percent) will be designated as workforce housing. Miami-Dade County defines workforce housing as housing for households earning within 60 to 140 percent of the area median income (AMI).
Miami-Dade County’s median household income was $87,200 as of May 2025.
Residences at Spoke Aventura will range from studio to three-bedroom units, measuring about 530 to 1,820 square feet each. Amenities will include a resort-style swimming pool, indoor gym, and padel court.
In addition to the residences at Spoke Aventura, plans also call for 3,000 square feet of retail and 435 parking spots. Group P6 is the developer. The firm recently secured $140 million in construction financing to bring this project to completion. RXR was the lender.
Moss & Associates is the general contractor. The firm intends to start construction on Spoke Aventura in the coming months and have the project completed by 2028. IDEA Architecture is the architect.
Spoke Aventura is planned for 2600 N.E. 203rd Street, Miami, Florida, 33180 , in Miami-Dade County. It will occupy a 1.4-acre site purchased for $16.07 million in 2024.
items.desc: Florida YIMBY says "Yes In My Backyard" to positive new development in Florida.

items.title: 1836: Dade County is created
items.desc: Dade County was created on February 4, 1836, named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. That same year, Fort Dallas was built and served as a military base during the Second Seminole War.
